## Delta (9i)

- **F84-1:** exactly one anchor per endpoint. `anchor_of` now maps endpoint -> `(when, machine_record_key)`: the
  newest `class == "ok"` row, ties on `when` broken by the greater record key (lexicographic, so deterministic across

  unchanged otherwise.

  production path with the real `open_exclusive` journal lock: 497 distinct recent anchors + three equal-`when` Y
  successes (distinct repos, hence keys); X's pair in the journal only; journal held; X's success added (when after
  the pair, before the fillers) -> X's success persisted, rows <= 500; still held, a newer Y success -> X's success
  still persisted; released; an unrelated update applies the journal -> X 0 hits / available.
- Residual, documented not fixed: more than 500 distinct endpoints each with a live anchor still evict the oldest
  anchors (the 500-row file is the plugin-shared format limit).

## 9e - the second acceptance pass (handoff 76: F76-1)

**F76-1 (blocker):** the 9d read-time bound was an unconditional 24 h age filter applied in
`endpoint_health` (`CAP_PAIR_MAX_AGE_MINUTES`). A hinted entry exhausted on 2026-10-14 and declaring a
reset of 2026-10-26 was wrongly reported "available" again two days later, because both hits aged out
of the 24 h window although the declared cap period had not reset. Rule: a hit is pair evidence only
while it lies inside the entry's CURRENT cap period - a hinted entry's hit counts iff the reset that
follows it has not passed (`next_cap_reset(hint, hit) > now`), an unhinted entry's hit counts iff it is
younger than 24 h at read time (the 9d rule, unchanged). `until` is unchanged (hinted ->
`next_cap_reset(hint, second)`, unhinted -> first hit + 24 h), and rows without a `consult_id` still
take no part. `endpoint_health` now retains id-carrying hits up to a generous fixed bound
(`CAP_PAIR_RETENTION_MINUTES`, 35 days - the longest monthly period) and `plan_cap_verdict` applies the
per-entry period rule, which keeps the verdict identical across every reader (providers table,
preflight, `plan_verdict`) independent of retention. A pair lying entirely before the last reset is no
evidence. Tests: the RC1 case (hinted stays out at 2026-10-16, available after 2026-10-26 16:00) and
the hinted/unhinted split of the 25 h-old pair in `plan::the_cap_policy_is_inferred_exhaustion_with_a_24_hour_probe`
and `plan::hits_are_counted_by_consultation_identity_not_by_time`.

## 9f - the third acceptance pass (handoff 78: F78-1, F78-2)

**F78-1 (blocker):** the detector fixed `second = hits[0]` (the newest in-period hit) and looked for a
partner within 60 min of IT only, so a later ISOLATED instant 429 (a third distinct consultation at
22:00Z after a 20:00/20:20Z pair, read at 22:11Z) hid the established pair and the exhausted entry read
available before its declared reset. Fix: `plan_cap_verdict` now scans all retained distinct-id
in-period hits newest-first and takes the newest QUALIFYING pair (any two within 60 min) for
`second`/`first`/`until`/`gap_min`. **F78-2 (blocker):** `update_machine_health` retention kept a row
only while `recent` (<= 24 h) or `still_out`, so id-carrying instant-429 evidence was pruned once its
ordinary burst `until` expired - a reader in ANOTHER repository (no ledger copies of its own) then lost
the pair before the declared reset, and the 35-day `CAP_PAIR_RETENTION_MINUTES` only filtered rows
already loaded. Fix: retention now keeps an id-carrying instant-429 row (`consult_id` non-empty, class
`quota`, kind `burst` - exactly what `endpoint_health` counts, since `machine_endpoint_consults` mirrors
it with `finished_at == when`) for `CAP_PAIR_RETENTION_MINUTES` regardless of `until`, and the
500-record cap (`cap_machine_endpoints`) evicts non-evidence rows first and the oldest evidence rows
only when none are left. The replay guard is unaffected (evidence keys merely persist longer). Tests:
the RC1 isolated-hit case in `plan::the_cap_policy_is_inferred_exhaustion_with_a_24_hour_probe`, and the
production-path RC2 (`health::machine_health_retention_keeps_cap_evidence_until_the_period_ends`) plus
the cap-ordering unit test `health::the_record_cap_evicts_cap_evidence_last`.

## 9g - the fourth acceptance pass (handoff 80: F80-1)

**F80-1 (blocker):** 9f retention was asymmetric. A cap-evidence row (id-carrying quota/burst) lives
35 days and is evicted LAST, but the usable reply that CLEARS it - the one `endpoint_health`'s
`newest_ok` uses to suppress older cap candidates - got only the 24 h `recent` window and was evicted
FIRST by `cap_machine_endpoints`. A machine-only reader (another repository, no ledger copies) then saw
the surviving pair without its clearing success and falsely reinstated the hinted refusal until the
declared reset. Two triggers: an unrelated update > 25 h after the success pruned the success and kept
the pair; or 500 evidence rows plus the clearing success, where the cap evicted the success at once.
Fix (durable, not a watermark): in `update_machine_health`, after merging and BEFORE retention and the
cap, for every endpoint fingerprint the newest clearing success (`is_clearing_success` - a `class ==
"ok"` row, which `machine_endpoint_consults` mirrors as the `"usable reply"` outcome `is_usable_outcome`
accepts) DROPS every evidence row of that endpoint whose `when` is not newer than it. Dropping (rather
than clearing `consult_id`) is durable and matches how the cap/retention already evict rows; the
journal's applied marks still bar resurrection (they are written from `j_records`, not from survivors,
as the cap-eviction replay test already proves). Consequence: with both time retention and the record
cap, an endpoint never keeps evidence older than its newest clearing success, while the ledger-side
reader is unchanged. Test: the production-path RC1
`health::machine_health_drops_evidence_superseded_by_a_clearing_success` (success at +48 h, success
under cap pressure, and the no-success pair still held).

## 9h - the fifth acceptance pass (handoff 82: F82-1)

**F82-1 (blocker):** 9g's supersede only sees evidence already merged. If a cap pair sits in a journal
held exclusively past the update's 20 x 50 ms open retries, that update continues WITHOUT reading it
and writes no applied marks; meanwhile the clearing success it adds is non-evidence, so the record cap
(or the 24 h `recent` window) evicts the success. A later update reads the journal, appends the pair,
finds no success to supersede it, and the pair survives the cap - an obsolete refusal until the declared
reset. The same gap covers delayed direct retries and later journal appends of old evidence. Fix (no new
schema field, the file is shared with the plugin): the NEWEST clearing success of each endpoint is a
durable CLEARING ANCHOR (`anchor_of` -> `endpoint -> when`, computed once and reused). The anchor is
protected like cap evidence - retention keeps it for `CAP_PAIR_RETENTION_MINUTES` (35 days) regardless
of `recent`, and `cap_machine_endpoints` now evicts in three tiers: non-protected first, then cap
evidence oldest-by-`when`, then the anchors oldest-by-`when` - so an endpoint's older evidence always
goes before its anchor and a lone old anchor outlives newer filler evidence. The supersede step stays
where it is (after merge, before retention and cap), so late-arriving evidence is dropped on the update
that merges it. Residuals (stated, not fixed): the plugin's own writer of the shared file applies its
own retention (cross-tool parity is out of this range); evidence older than 35 days is ignored by the
reader anyway. Test: the production-path RC1 with the real exclusive journal lock
`health::machine_health_anchor_supersedes_evidence_from_a_skipped_journal` (success added while the pair
waits in a held journal -> available after replay; and no success -> the refusal holds), plus the
cap-tier unit test `health::the_record_cap_keeps_the_anchor_over_older_evidence`.
